quote:
Quite a few  criticisms that are separate from the incel-adjacent posts.

1. Obviously FPS is an issue with performance. But the bigger issue this creates is seen when objects are in motion. As XQC said in a clip, driving or running around was giving him a headache when he was trying to look at the game, and that's been the case for many others as well.

2. Another one is that the story and dialogue of the leads seems pretty cookie-cutter. It has neither the narrative weight of GTA 4 or Red Dead, or the antics of GTA 5 that made it entertaining to watch.

3. Simply just way too many chores for what GTA has been in the past. Yes there have been chores, but not to an extent where it's significant at the beginning of the game, and to where it's more Red Dead than GTA. This not only results in a lack of a hook, which is why some are saying they're bored, but it also shifts the game away from having the GTA tone that many expected.

4. There are issues with the game environment, which is significant because that is being held up by journalists as the main reason for why it's reviewing so well (especially the realism aspect). Obviously there have been lots of bugs and clipping recorded, but there are also things like the exact same NPCs spawning next to each other despite it being advertised as rare, or punching a car resulting in it going flying - touching a pot plant destroying a car -things like this.

Hope this helps.
